title: Atomic change notes + reasoning (batching & cache refactor)
body:
Quick context:
- Large PR that lands a new continuous-batching path + small rewrite of prefix/KV cache invalidation logic. Goal: reduce tail latency for short requests (<=64 tokens) while preserving throughput for long sequences.
- Author: @diego-m, pair: @lina. Patch touches runtime scheduler, request routing, and one operator in the aten-like kernel layer.

High-level hypotheses (what I'll watch for in review):
1) Latency win on 1-64 token paths without regression in 256+ workloads. Expect 10-25% p99 improvement for short tokens when batching is warmed.
2) No correctness regressions from cache invalidation change (race on concurrent prefix updates).
3) No amplification of GPU memory fragmentation or KV cache leaks under high churn.

Design notes worth preserving in review comments:
- The new batcher uses a lightweight shared queue per-GPU + soft deadlines. This trades off batching depth for predictable latency; ensure we call this out in the runtime docs.
- Cache invalidation now timestamps per-namespace instead of per-request tokens; simpler GC semantics but need to ensure cross-model pinning doesn't evict active KV frames.
- Kernel change is intentionally non-invasive: same op signature, different internal sharding for attention state.

Checklist for code review (atomic items):
- Correctness:
  - [ ] Verify unit tests exist for cache eviction scenarios (concurrent writes + reads). Check test names: cache_eviction_race_*, prefix_invalidation_ordering_*.
  - [ ] Confirm added assertions only enabled in debug (no CLANG_ASAN-like expensive checks in release).
- Performance/regression:
  - [ ] Run microbench: short-sequence p50/p95/p99 before/after on same hardware (small VM with A10x). Capture tokens/sec and memory usage.
  - [ ] Check for added allocations in hot path (heap allocs per-token). Grep for malloc/new in changed files.
- Observability and telemetry:
  - [ ] New metrics: batch_wait_ms, batch_depth_hist, kv_gc_pause_ms — ensure they are emitted and documented.
  - [ ] Validation that tags/labels for metric cardinality are bounded (no request-id tags).
- Safety and deployment:
  - [ ] Feature-flag gating present (runtime flag + console toggle). Confirm default is off for Dedicated & Private.
  - [ ] Canary rollout plan in PR description (percentages, duration, rollback condition thresholds).
- API/compat:
  - [ ] No change to public API surface (SDKs) — validate codegen and proto compatibility.
  - [ ] Migration notes for model variants that relied on old cache semantics.

Local test plan notes (what I will run before approving):
- Unit: run new cache suite (./bazel test //runtime/...:cache_tests).
- Integration: launch a small cluster from release branch + patch; run our perf harness with 1k qps synthetic mix (80% short, 20% long). Compare logs for cache hits, batch sizes, tail latencies.
- Fuzz: quick fuzz on concurrent prefix updates to try to reproduce race.

Rollback & mitigations (if something goes wrong in canary):
- Immediate: flip feature flag to previous batching path (control plane toggle).
- If toggle fails: revert canary nodes to last stable image (image tag pinned in rollout).
- Postmortem triggers: >2x increase in 'kv_gc_pause_ms' or unexplained p99 jump for any customer route.

Questions for the author (to request inline):
- Why choose timestamp-based eviction vs simple generation counters? Was cross-model reuse evaluated?
- Is there a scenario where a model pins a KV frame for long-running sessions and we accidentally evict due to namespace TTL?
- The new queue uses a mutex per-GPU; did you consider lock-free SPSC queues for lower contention? Any benchmark data?

Follow-ups / follow-through items (post-merge):
- Add a small console dashboard (perf + cache metrics) to the rollout checklist.
- Add a short runbook snippet in SRE playbook describing the feature-flag and rollback steps.
- Schedule a short post-rollout review with Lina and runtime SRE to capture observed vs expected gains.

Notes to self (messy):
- Keep a copy of perf results in /tmp/atomic-batch-2026-02-22 before clearing.
- Add GH review comment suggesting small helper to centralize timestamp logic (avoid duplicate logic in 3 files).
- Remember to check dedicated perf on c5-ish instances (lower GPU count) — behavior sometimes different.

TL;DR for reviewer comment: focus on cache correctness (concurrency + retention), metric hygiene, and deployment guardrails. If those are solid, the p99 wins are compelling and worth landing behind a feature flag.

----
Recent quick captures (logs / numbers I pasted here while iterating):
- local synthetic: short p99 92ms -> 68ms (with batch warm), long p99 unchanged ~420ms.
- observed batch_depth mean: 6.2, p95: 15. Had spikes to 40 during warmup.
- KV GC pause sample: 1.2ms median, 38ms max (need to understand worst-case outliers).

End of notes.
